concept: Engineering-metaphor vocabulary tics in LLM output
summary: Source-anchored research for Engineering-metaphor vocabulary tics in LLM output. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Practitioner glossaries describe the engineering-metaphor tic as models importing engineering language into ordinary life: leverage for use, unpack as the conversational cousin of delve, plus optimize, streamline, facilitate, harness, and promoting observations into pillars, layers, stages, dimensions. (low confidence)

The cause of lexical overrepresentation is unresolved: Juzek and Ward found no evidence for architecture, algorithm or training-data causes; model testing is consistent with RLHF playing a role, but an exploratory human study gave mixed results. (medium confidence)

Excess-word analysis of over 15 million PubMed abstracts (2010-2024) found an abrupt post-ChatGPT rise of style words (delve, underscore, crucial, pivotal, utilize, align), implying at least 13.5% of 2024 abstracts were LLM-processed, up to 40% in some subcorpora. (high confidence)

A 2026 study of 160,000 responses from 8 frontier models (data collected 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-15) lists leverage, robust, streamline, holistic, landscape, foster among overused vocabulary; its Verbal Tic Index ranged from 0.295 (DeepSeek V3.2) to 0.590 (Gemini 3.1 Pro), and tic rates rose about 110% between conversation turn 1 and turn 20. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23)

Word-list detection is contested: commentators attribute delve-style vocabulary to formal Nigerian business English of outsourced RLHF annotators, and vocabulary-based detectors risk false positives on formal or non-Western English. (low confidence)

Quantitative studies mostly measure generic style words (delve, tapestry, intrinsic, crucial); no source found quantifies the engineering-metaphor subset (load-bearing, scaffolding, surface, anchor) separately, so claims that these are LLM-specific rest on anecdote. (low confidence)
